edges.description: SERAC1 dysfunction alters cellular PG remodeling, supported by complementation.
Reduced BMP is observed in SERAC1-deficient cells; the intervening remodeling steps remain incompletely defined.
Patient cells associate loss of SERAC1 with network fragmentation; mediation by individual lipid changes has not been isolated.
Patient cells and liver tissue show abnormal cristae.
Patient fibroblasts show impaired cytoplasm-to-mitochondria calcium buffering.
Experimental SERAC1 loss impairs SFXN1-mediated transport.
Altered PG substrate composition is linked to altered cardiolipin species.
Altered cardiolipin is a proposed contributor to respiratory dysfunction; the disease-specific intervening assembly steps are unresolved.
The discovery study links low BMP to abnormal intracellular cholesterol handling.
The authors propose this sequence; a selective calcium-rescue experiment is not established by the available abstract.
Reduced mitochondrial serine supply impairs the one-carbon pathway in the experimental model.
The study links impaired one-carbon metabolism with insufficient nucleotide supply.
Insufficient nucleotide supply limits maintenance of mtDNA in the experimental systems.
Rescue of mtDNA and mitochondrial function supports a contribution of nucleotide-limited mtDNA maintenance; intermediate respiratory-subunit effects are not resolved by the abstract.
Respiratory-chain abnormalities can impair oxidative phosphorylation.
Mitochondrial dysfunction is a proposed contributor to selective basal-ganglia injury; the basis of selective vulnerability is unresolved.
Mitochondrial abnormalities coexist with infantile liver disease; the tissue-injury steps are not fully established.
Hearing impairment is a clinical consequence associated with SERAC1 deficiency; its anatomical and molecular basis remains uncertain.
MEGDEL belongs to the secondary acidurias associated with mitochondrial phospholipid dysfunction; the exact route to organic-acid accumulation is unresolved.
Lactate elevation accompanies some episodes of mitochondrial dysfunction.
Basal-ganglia injury is a plausible contributor to dystonia, but clinical coexistence does not establish the full circuit mechanism.
The structural injury is expressed as the evolving MRI abnormality.
Patient-cell PG abnormalities and their partial normalization by wild-type SERAC1 directly connect SERAC1 dysfunction to lipid remodeling.
edges.limitations: Fibroblast findings do not establish tissue-specific neuronal, auditory or hepatic pathology.

edges.description: A severe neonatal patient line shows a severely fragmented mitochondrial network and altered cristae morphology as distinct structural findings.
edges.limitations: The measurements come from a single patient line carrying one severe truncating allele, so allelic and interindividual variation in these structural phenotypes is unknown.

edges.description: The same severe neonatal patient line shows deficient cytoplasm-to-mitochondria calcium buffering, a functional finding distinct from the structural network and cristae changes.
edges.limitations: The measurement comes from a single patient line carrying one severe truncating allele, so allelic and interindividual variation in calcium handling is unknown, and fibroblast calcium buffering does not establish the equivalent defect in neurons or hair cells.

edges.description: The mouse reproduces mtDNA depletion and the biochemical diagnostic phenotype, and nucleoside supplementation restores mtDNA content.
edges.limitations: The accessible source is an abstract. It does not resolve which lipid abnormalities or stage-specific human MRI lesions were reproduced, nor the contribution of each pathway to human disease. Preclinical rescue does not establish clinical efficacy or safety.

edges.description: Affected dogs lose neurons from the putamen and caudate nucleus, the same striatal targets damaged in human MEGDEL, and develop a progressive movement disorder.
edges.limitations: Published canine neuropathology includes Purkinje-cell, striatal and nigral neuronal loss with ataxia and tremor. Hearing and cognition were not assessed, and hepatic or urine organic-acid phenotyping was not reported. These are untested features, not established absences. The paper does not demonstrate canine lipid, serine-transport or mtDNA abnormalities.

edges.description: LPGAT1-deficient cells and mice connect PG remodeling and mitochondrial PG transport, with a PG34:1/PG36:1 shift resembling SERAC1 deficiency.
edges.limitations: The perturbed gene is LPGAT1. Cardiomyopathy and mortality in these mice cannot be generalized to human SERAC1 disease. Precise PHB/TIM lipid-transfer activity remains unresolved.

edges.description: A raised PG34:1/PG36:1 ratio is the direct cellular measurement of the remodeling defect.

nodes.description: Hearing aids and cochlear implants have been used, but expected benefit should be discussed with audiology and the family. In a 36-person retrospective hearing study, 22 received hearing aids and six subsequently received implants; only one implanted individual acquired spoken language, which became less clear with progression. Improved environmental interaction can still be meaningful. The auditory lesion is not consistently localized.
